expectations.text: Output contains a fenced mermaid sequenceDiagram block that parses cleanly — verified with mermaid-cli (exit 0) where the CLI is available, otherwise by syntax review against references/syntax.md, with the grader stating which of the two checks it actually ran
expectations.evidence: Check run: hosted Mermaid MCP (mcp__mermaid__validate_and_render_mermaid_diagram), permitted for this eval; mermaid-cli is not installed. The block reached the renderer with no parse error — the server returned only 'Generated PNG exceeds size limit of 512000 bytes' (an output-byte cap hit by the very wide notes), i.e. Mermaid parsed and laid the diagram out. Contrast control: feeding deliberately broken input (`A ~~> B: y`) to the same tool returns 'Parse error on line 6: ... Expecting NEWLINE, ... got INVALID', a different failure class. A structurally identical trim of the same diagram also returned only the size message, never a parse error. Manual review against references/syntax.md agrees: `>` is avoided via '(gt 0)', activations balance (one `+` each for API/PG/DB against `DB-->>-API` and trailing `deactivate PG` / `deactivate API` after the alt `end`), 3-branch alt closed once.

expectations.text: The real flow from the code is shown: POST /orders -> PayGate POST /v2/charges -> Postgres INSERT -> RabbitMQ order.created publish, with 201 on success

RETURNING id' (db.py:19-21); 'API-)MQ: publish order.created' (events.py:24 routing_key="order.created"); 'API-->>C: 201 Created'.
